In current SCOPe 2.08 the collagen-binding domain was moved into the Galactose-binding domain-like superfamily as new family b.18.1.36 'Collagen-binding domain' (family sunid 267607; protein 'Class 1 collagenase' 267633; species Clostridium histolyticum 267693), so d1nqda_ and d1dlca1 now share superfamily b.18.1 but remain in different families (b.18.1.36 vs b.18.1.3). compare_scop_domains reports the relationship as same_superfamily, lowest shared node b.18.1 sunid 49785, with no caveats. SCOPe superfamily membership denotes probable common ancestry inferred from structure and function rather than detectable sequence similarity; family-level (clear sequence-based) homology is not asserted. Structural evidence: both domains are jelly-roll beta-sandwich modules with the galactose-binding domain-like (lectin-like) topology; curators judged the ColG CBD core strand arrangement fits b.18 better than CUB-like, and the b.18.1.36 family annotation cites PubMed 17977833 as describing likely homology between d2quoa_, d1w99a3 and d1nqdb_, i.e. structure-based remote homology detection drove the reclassification. Functional evidence: both are non-catalytic surface-binding modules appended to larger proteins; the ColG CBD binds calcium (1nqd 'complexed with ca') and collagen, and Cry3A domain III is the toxin's receptor/carbohydrate recognition module (family mapped to Pfam PF03944), consistent with the ligand-binding role typical of the galactose-binding domain-like superfamily. Limits: the relationship is superfamily-level only, so specific function must not be transferred (ColG collagen/calcium binding does not imply Cry3A binds collagen, and toxin receptor specificity does not transfer to ColG); sequence identity is negligible so neither is a safe homology-modelling template for the other without independent structure-alignment support; the FATCAT structure-hit stream for chain 1nqdA was empty because hits are stored only for its 90% cluster representative 1nqjA, so a pairwise structural alignment was not independently verified here. Note also that 1nqd chain B is now split into d1nqdb1 (B:893-1008, b.18.1.36) and a small l.1.1.1 fragment d1nqdb2 (B:891-892), whereas in 2.04 it was a single domain d1nqdb_.
